Data Extraction
Data were extracted in two ways:

Area-level indicators (R1, R2, R1_2 by department within Areas 05 and 06): Manually transcribed from the PDF report into vqr_area_data.csv. The pipeline script also includes a PDF parsing function (parse_area_tables()) using pdftools and regex, though the verified CSV is used by default.
Department-level indicators (all 32 departments): Transcribed into vqr_ird_data.csv from Table 2.4 of the institutional report.







WarningData extraction caveats




R1 data for Area 05 includes only 5 of the 7 departments. BCA and DNS are excluded because they had fewer than 10 expected products from tenured staff — an ANVUR reporting threshold, not a data gap.
All R1 values were added from pages 11–12 of the ANVUR PDF during the analysis. The values should be cross-checked against the original source.

title: Data & Methods
text:
Indicator Definitions

Quality indicator R
The R indicator for a department in a given area is:
\[
R = \frac{\bar{v}_{\text{dept}}}{\bar{v}_{\text{national}}}
\]
where \[\bar{v}\] is the average evaluation score of submitted products. R > 1 means the department’s average quality exceeds the national average for that area.


Size-weight indicator H
\[
H = \frac{n_{\text{dept}}}{N_{\text{institution}}}
\]
where \[n_{\text{dept}}\] is the number of expected products from the department and \[N_{\text{institution}}\] is the total across the institution. H reflects the department’s relative contribution to the institution’s evaluated output.


Composite indicator IRD
\[
IRD = H \times R
\]
This product means that IRD scales with both quality (R) and size (H). A small department with high R can still have a low IRD, because H is small. This is a deliberate design choice by ANVUR: IRD is intended to capture total research impact, not quality per capita.






ImportantCritical note on IRD interpretation



IRD is sometimes used in internal benchmarking as though it measures departmental “performance.” This is misleading. A department with R = 1.26 (top quality) but only 157 expected products will always score lower on IRD than a department with R = 1.05 but 350 products. IRD reflects departmental scale as much as — or more than — research quality. This is explored in detail in the Results.

title: VQR 2020–2024: Performance of the Department of Molecular Medicine (DMM)
text:
The Valutazione della Qualità della Ricerca (VQR) 2020–2024 is the Italian national research quality assessment exercise conducted by ANVUR (Agenzia Nazionale di Valutazione del Sistema Universitario e della Ricerca). It evaluates the quality of research outputs produced by Italian universities and research institutions over a five-year period.
Results were published on 28 May 2026. This report provides a transparent, reproducible analysis of how the Department of Molecular Medicine (DMM) at the Università degli Studi di Padova performed relative to peer departments within the university and nationally.


ANVUR evaluates departments using three families of indicators:








Indicator
Definition
Interpretation




R (quality)
Ratio of a department’s average evaluation score to the national area average
R > 1 means above-average quality


H (size-weight)
Fraction of expected products contributed by the department
Reflects the department’s share of evaluated output


IRD (composite)
Product of H × R
Captures both quality and quantity — rewards large departments with high quality



These are computed separately for three personnel categories:

R1: Tenured staff (personale a tempo indeterminato)
R2: Newly recruited / promoted staff (neo-assunti / avanzamenti di carriera)
R1_2: All evaluated staff combined







NoteWhy does this matter?



VQR results directly influence the allocation of research funding (Fondo di Finanziamento Ordinario, FFO) to Italian universities, and are used internally for departmental benchmarking and strategic planning. A department’s VQR performance has concrete financial and reputational consequences.

title: VQR 2020–2024: Performance of the Department of Molecular Medicine (DMM)
text:
Executive Summary

DMM demonstrates strong research quality but is penalised by size in the composite IRD ranking.

DMM ranks 1st out of 32 departments for R1 quality (1.26) — the best among all Padova departments for tenured-staff research quality.
For overall quality (R1_2 = 1.15), DMM ranks 4th out of 32 — solidly in the top tier.
However, because DMM is a relatively small department (157 expected products), its composite IRD1_2 (0.11) ranks only 21st out of 32.
This reflects a structural property of the IRD indicator: it scales with department size, so even high-quality small departments receive low IRD scores.

Data Notes

R1 rows were missing from the original CSV for most departments. They were manually extracted from pages 11–12 of the raw ANVUR PDF and added during this session.

vqr_ird_data.csv

Covers all 32 departments at Università di Padova. ✅
Used for the IRD ranking, IRD scatter, and the three-panel R1/R2/R1_2 ranking chart.

Key Fixes Made to vqr_pipeline.R

CSV delimiter — changed read_csv → read_delim(..., delim = ";") (files are semicolon-separated).
Department name spacing — corrected the sigle lookup dictionary to match exact punctuation in the CSV (e.g., "SCIENZE CARDIO- TORACO-" not "SCIENZE CARDIO - TORACO -").
Area code format — CSV uses 5/6, not "05"/"06"; updated plot_area() calls accordingly.
Palette name collision — c(DMM_R1 = RED["R1"]) produced keys like DMM_R1.R1; fixed with unname().
Missing R1 data — extracted R1 rows for Areas 05 and 06 from the raw ANVUR PDF and added to vqr_area_data.csv.
DMM label highlighting — ggtext::element_markdown() does not render HTML/CSS in saved PNGs in this environment (ggtext 0.1.2 limitation). Workaround: axis.text.y = element_blank() + geom_text() with color and fontface aesthetics. Applied to rank_R1_R2_R12_R.png and ird_rank_R.png.
Rank panel — replaced broken facet_wrap + coord_flip approach with three independent plots combined via patchwork. Rank computation uses ties.method = "first" to match ANVUR ordering (DMM: R1=1°, R2=6°, R1_2=4° su 32).
IRD rank chart — added red bold DMM label, dark border on DMM bar, red title, tightened x-axis limits.
IRD scatter — added multi-line DMM annotation with arrow, labelled DFA/DII/DSB/DiBio/BCA, added trend line label, completed title with “(numero di docenti)”.

Project Overview
This is an R-based analysis pipeline for VQR (Valutazione Qualità della Ricerca - Italian Research Quality Assessment) 2020-2024 data from the University of Padova (UNIPD). The project specifically focuses on the Department of Molecular Medicine (DMM) but includes comparative analysis across 32 departments and 2 main research areas.

The fill mapping should be using the grp column constructed as paste0(ifelse(is_dmm, "DMM_", "ALT_"), indicatore), which would create DMM_R2 and DMM_R1_2 that should map to red tones in the palette. I’m wondering if the issue is with how the factor levels interact with position_dodge — since indicatore has R1, R2, and R1_2 but DMM only has R2 and R1_2, the positioning might be off. Or the palette mapping itself might not be matching correctly between the named palette entries and the actual grp values being used. Ah, I see the issue now—when I nest the named vectors like that, R concatenates the names together, so I’m getting DMM_R1.R1 instead of just DMM_R1. I need to strip the names from the RED and GRAY values first, either by using unname() or accessing them as plain strings. 

Found it — the DMM has no R1 data, and there’s a naming bug in the palette. When you do c(DMM_R1 = RED["R1"]), R concatenates names to produce DMM_R1.R1 instead of DMM_R1. Let me fix the plot_area function:








































All 5 figures are now generated correctly with DMM highlighted in red. Here’s a summary of the three bugs I fixed in vqr_pipeline.R:

CSV delimiter — read_csv → read_delim(..., delim = ";") since the data files are semicolon-separated

title: Results
text: This page presents all key figures from the analysis of DMM’s VQR 2020–2024 results. Each figure is generated from the embedded R code (click “Code” to expand). Source data: ANVUR institutional report for the Università degli Studi di Padova, Tables 2.1–2.4.

title: Results
text:
Area-Level Comparisons
DMM contributes evaluated products in two disciplinary areas: Area 05 (Biology) and Area 06 (Medicine). The following figures compare DMM against other Padova departments active in each area, across all three R indicators.

Area 05 — Biology


Code
plot_area <- function(area_code, titolo) {
  d <- area_df |> filter(area == area_code)
  ord <- d |> filter(indicatore == "R1_2") |> arrange(desc(R)) |> pull(sigla)
  ord <- union(ord, unique(d$sigla))
  d <- d |> mutate(
    sigla = factor(sigla, levels = ord),
    grp = paste0(ifelse(is_dmm, "DMM_", "ALT_"), indicatore)
  )
  pal <- c(
    DMM_R1 = unname(RED["R1"]), DMM_R2 = unname(RED["R2"]),
    DMM_R1_2 = unname(RED["R1_2"]),
    ALT_R1 = unname(GRAY["R1"]), ALT_R2 = unname(GRAY["R2"]),
    ALT_R1_2 = unname(GRAY["R1_2"])
  )
  ggplot(d, aes(sigla, R, group = indicatore, fill = grp)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = REF_LINE) +
    geom_text(aes(label = it_num(R)),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = titolo, x = NULL,
         y = "R indicator (> 1 = above national average)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        face = ifelse(levels(d$sigla) == "DMM", "bold", "plain")
      )
    )
}
plot_area("5", "Area 05 — Biology: DMM vs peer departments")








Figure 1: R indicators for Padova departments in Area 05 (Biology). DMM in red; peers in grey. Dashed line = national average (R = 1.0). BCA and DNS are excluded from R1 because they had < 10 expected products from tenured staff.





In Area 05, DMM’s R1 (1.12) is above the national average, though not the highest among Padova biology departments — DIMED leads with 1.31 (albeit from a small base of only 10 products). DMM’s R2 (1.12) and R1_2 (1.12) are consistent: above-average but mid-range within this peer group. DiBio, the largest biology department, outperforms on R2 (1.19) and R1_2 (1.15).


Area 06 — Medicine


Code
plot_area("6", "Area 06 — Medicine: DMM vs peer departments")








Figure 2: R indicators for Padova departments in Area 06 (Medicine). DMM in red; peers in grey. Dashed line = national average (R = 1.0).





In Area 06, DMM stands out more clearly. Its R1 of 1.45 is the highest among all Padova medicine departments — a substantial margin over the next-best (DSB at 1.25). R2 (1.11) and R1_2 (1.20) remain above average, though DSB surpasses DMM on these metrics (R2 = 1.37, R1_2 = 1.36). DMM’s strength in Area 06 appears to be driven particularly by the quality of its tenured-staff research output.

title: Results
text:
University-Wide Rankings

R1, R2, and R1_2 across all 32 departments


Code
dmm_vals_rank <- ird_df |>
  mutate(across(c(R1, R2, R1_2),
                \(x) rank(desc(x), ties.method = "first"), .names = "rk_{.col}")) |>
  filter(is_dmm) |>
  select(R1, R2, R1_2, rk_R1, rk_R2, rk_R1_2)

panel_labels_rank <- c(
  R1 = paste0("R1 — tenured staff\nDMM: ",
              it_num(dmm_vals_rank$R1), " — ",
              dmm_vals_rank$rk_R1, "th of 32"),
  R2 = paste0("R2 — newly recruited/promoted\nDMM: ",
              it_num(dmm_vals_rank$R2), " — ",
              dmm_vals_rank$rk_R2, "th of 32"),
  R1_2 = paste0("R1_2 — all staff\nDMM: ",
                it_num(dmm_vals_rank$R1_2), " — ",
                dmm_vals_rank$rk_R1_2, "th of 32")
)

make_rank_panel <- function(col, color, strip_title) {
  d <- ird_df |>
    transmute(R = .data[[col]], is_dmm,
              lbl_fct = fct_reorder(sigla, R),
              fill = ifelse(is_dmm, color, "#B0B0B0"))
  ggplot(d, aes(x = R, y = lbl_fct, fill = fill)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.78) +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = -0.04, y = lbl_fct, label = as.character(lbl_fct),
          color = is_dmm, fontface = ifelse(is_dmm, "bold", "plain")),
      hjust = 1, size = 2.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = it_num(R)), hjust = -0.08, size = 2.0, color = INK) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = REF_LINE, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "gray30", "TRUE" = "#9B0014"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1.4, 0.2), limits = c(-0.05, 1.52),
                       labels = function(x) ifelse(x < 0, "", it_num(x)),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(title = strip_title, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9.5) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(color = "#9B0014", face = "bold",
                                size = 8.5, lineheight = 1.2),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 4, r = 8, b = 4, l = 55)
    )
}

(
  make_rank_panel("R1", unname(RED["R1"]), panel_labels_rank["R1"]) |
  make_rank_panel("R2", unname(RED["R2"]), panel_labels_rank["R2"]) |
  make_rank_panel("R1_2", unname(RED["R1_2"]), panel_labels_rank["R1_2"])
) + plot_annotation(
  title = "DMM position among Padova departments — R1, R2, R1_2",
  caption = "Values from Table 2.4 (aggregated across areas)  ·  Dashed line = national average R = 1.0  ·  DMM in red",
  theme = theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#9B0014", face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, color = "gray40")
  )
)








Figure 3: All 32 Padova departments ranked by R1, R2, and R1_2 (aggregated across disciplinary areas, Table 2.4). DMM highlighted in red. Dashed line = national average (R = 1.0).





DMM’s ranking varies substantially across the three indicators:

The gap between R1 (1.26) and R2 (1.11) suggests that DMM’s tenured faculty produce higher-quality research than its more recently recruited staff — or alternatively, that newly recruited researchers have not yet had sufficient time to build a mature publication portfolio within the evaluation window.

    legend.position = "right",
    legend.key.height = unit(1.8, "cm"),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 6.5, color = "gray40"),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 4, r = 8, b = 4, l = 55)
  )








Figure 4: All 32 departments ranked by IRD1_2. Bar colour encodes R1_2 quality (green = above average, red = below). DMM (bold red label, dark border) ranks 21st despite having R1_2 = 1.15.





This figure reveals the central tension in the VQR results: DMM has one of the highest R1_2 values (green bar), yet ranks in the bottom third on IRD. This is because IRD = H × R, and H is proportional to department size. Departments like DFA (387 expected products) or FISPPA (352) achieve high IRD even with modest R values, simply because they are large.


IRD vs department size


Code
dmm_sc <- ird_df |>
  mutate(rk_ird = rank(desc(IRD1_2), ties.method = "first"),
         rk_r12 = rank(desc(R1_2), ties.method = "first")) |>
  filter(is_dmm)

ann_x_sc <- 195; ann_y_sc <- 0.082
ann_lbl_sc <- paste0(
  "DMM  (R1_2=", it_num(dmm_sc$R1_2), " \u00b7 ",
  dmm_sc$rk_r12, "th for quality,\n",
  dmm_sc$rk_ird, "th for IRD out of 32)"
)

ggplot(ird_df, aes(n_attesi, IRD1_2)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE,
              linetype = "dashed", color = "#AAAAAA", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 130, y = 0.248,
           label = "Trend (IRD increases with size)",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.8, color = "gray50", fontface = "italic") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = R1_2), shape = 21, size = 4, color = "white") +
  geom_point(data = filter(ird_df, is_dmm),
             shape = 21, size = 6, color = "#9B0014", fill = NA, stroke = 1.5) +
  annotate("segment",
           x = ann_x_sc, xend = dmm_sc$n_attesi + 3,
           y = ann_y_sc + 0.003, yend = dmm_sc$IRD1_2 - 0.002,
           color = "#9B0014", linewidth = 0.6,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(5, "pt"), type = "closed")) +
  annotate("label",
           x = ann_x_sc, y = ann_y_sc,
           label = ann_lbl_sc,
           color = "#9B0014", fill = "white",
           label.color = "#9B0014", label.size = 0.4,
           size = 2.8, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, lineheight = 1.1) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(ird_df, sigla %in% c("DFA", "DII", "DSB", "DiBio", "BCA")),
    aes(label = sigla), size = 2.8, color = INK,
    nudge_y = 0.005, segment.color = "gray60", segment.size = 0.3,
    min.segment.length = 0.2, box.padding = 0.3, point.padding = 0.2,
    seed = 7481
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("#B2182B", "#F4A582", "#FFFFBF", "#A6D96A", "#1A9850"),
    values = rescale(c(0.90, 0.97, 1.00, 1.08, 1.20)),
    name = "R1_2 (quality)",
    breaks = c(0.95, 1.00, 1.05, 1.10, 1.15),
    limits = c(0.90, 1.20)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Why IRD depends on department size",
    x = "Department size — expected products (\u2248 number of faculty)",
    y = "IRD1_2 (composite indicator)",
    caption = "Source: ANVUR, VQR 2020–2024 — Università degli Studi di Padova, Table 2.4."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#9B0014", face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 6.5, color = "gray40"),
    legend.key.height = unit(1.6, "cm")
  )








Figure 5: IRD1_2 vs department size (number of expected products). The dashed trend line shows that IRD increases approximately linearly with size. DMM (circled) has high quality (R1_2 = 1.15, rank 4/32) but low IRD (rank 21/32) due to its relatively small size.





The scatter plot makes the structural relationship explicit: IRD is almost entirely determined by department size, with quality (colour) providing only modest variation around the trend line. DMM sits well below the trend line for its size, but this is because it is a smaller department.






ImportantImplications for benchmarking



Using IRD as the sole or primary metric for internal benchmarking disadvantages small departments regardless of their research quality. DMM ranks 1st on R1 and 4th on R1_2 among all 32 Padova departments, yet 21st on IRD. If funding or prestige decisions rely heavily on IRD, high-quality small departments are structurally penalised.
A fairer comparison would use R (quality per product) alongside IRD, or present IRD residuals after accounting for department size.

title: About
text: This website presents a transparent, reproducible analysis of the VQR 2020–2024 results for the Department of Molecular Medicine (DMM) at the Università degli Studi di Padova. It was created to facilitate informed discussion about the VQR indicators and their implications for departmental benchmarking.
